```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(

```

_theftdlc_ is an R package for analyzing, interpreting, and visualizing time-series features calculated with [_theft_](https://hendersontrent.github.io/theft/).
It covers data-quality checks, normalization, low-dimensional projections, clustering, feature selection, time-series classification, and statistical hypothesis testing for comparing feature sets.
_theftdlc_ is the "downloadable content" (DLC) for _theft_, just like the [DLC](https://en.bandainamcoent.eu/elden-ring/elden-ring/shadow-of-the-erdtree) you get for video games.

📖 **Full documentation:** [hendersontrent.github.io/theftdlc](https://hendersontrent.github.io/theftdlc/), including the vignette and function reference.
📄 **Paper:** ["Feature-Based Time-Series Analysis in R using the Theft Ecosystem"](https://journal.r-project.org/articles/RJ-2025-023/) describes the methods and walks through the full workflow.

## Installation

Install the stable version from CRAN:

```{r eval = FALSE}
install.packages("theftdlc")
```

Or install the development version from GitHub:

```{r eval = FALSE}
devtools::install_github("hendersontrent/theftdlc")
```

_theftdlc_ depends on [_theft_](https://github.com/hendersontrent/theft) (version 0.8.1 or later), which provides the `feature_calculations` objects that its functions take as input.
See the _theft_ README for how to install the Python-based feature sets that _theft_ can use.

## Functions

| Function | What it does |
|---|---|
| `plot()` | Plots a `feature_calculations` object (data quality, feature matrix, correlations, distributions), a projection from `project()`, or an interval summary from `interval()` |
| `project()` | Projects the feature matrix into two dimensions with PCA, MDS, t-SNE, or UMAP, after normalization |
| `cluster()` | Clusters time series using their feature vectors |
| `filter_duplicates()` | Removes duplicate features that exist in more than one feature set |
| `classify()` | Fits classifiers using features (by feature set or by individual feature) with a resampling approach, optionally with null models |
| `compare_features()` | Tests classification performance, comparing each set or feature against its null model, or against each other (pairwise), using the corrected resampled _t_-test of [_correctR_](https://github.com/hendersontrent/correctR) |
| `interval()` | Summarizes classification results with a measure of central tendency and an interval |
| `shrink()` | Selects features with a cross-validated penalized generalized linear model |

Features are normalized with [_normaliseR_](https://github.com/hendersontrent/normaliseR).
Older function names remain available as aliases: `tsfeature_classifier()` for `classify()`, `calculate_interval()` for `interval()`, and `reduce_dims()` for `project()`.

## The _theft_ ecosystem

Collectively, _theft_ and _theftdlc_ are the "_theft_ ecosystem".
_theft_ extracts features from seven feature sets (`"catch22"`, `"feasts"`, `"kats"`, `"tsfeatures"`, `"tsfresh"`, `"tsfel"`, and `"hctsa"`) and from any number of user-supplied features, and _theftdlc_ does everything after that.

<img src="man/figures/theft-packages.png" alt="Hex stickers of the theft and theftdlc packages for R" />

A high-level view of how the ecosystem is typically used:

<img src="man/figures/workflow-graphic_ecosystem-final.png" alt="Schematic of the theft ecosystem in R" />

Many more functions and options are available in the packages.

## Quick tour

_theft_ and _theftdlc_ combine into an efficient tidy workflow.
The code below calculates features using [_catch22_](https://github.com/hendersontrent/Rcatch22) and a custom set of the mean and standard deviation, then projects the feature space into two dimensions using principal components analysis:

```{r, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE, fig.height=6, fig.width=6}
library(dplyr)
library(theft)
library(theftdlc)

calculate_features(data = theft::simData, 
                   feature_set = "catch22",
                   features = list("mean" = mean, "sd" = sd)) %>%
  project(norm_method = "RobustSigmoid",
          unit_int = TRUE,
          low_dim_method = "PCA") %>%
  plot()
```

Here `calculate_features()` comes from _theft_, while `project()` and the `plot()` method come from _theftdlc_.

In the same way, we can compare the time-series classification performance of _catch22_ against our custom set of the first two moments:

```{r, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE}
calculate_features(data = theft::simData, 
                   feature_set = "catch22",
                   features = list("mean" = mean, "sd" = sd)) %>%
  classify(by_set = TRUE,
           n_resamples = 5,
           use_null = TRUE) %>%
  compare_features(by_set = TRUE,
                   hypothesis = "null") %>%
  head()
```

`classify()` and `compare_features()` come from _theftdlc_.

See the [vignette](https://hendersontrent.github.io/theftdlc/articles/theftdlc.html) for more information and the full functionality of both packages.
